metadata.question: In the Norwegian Sea during Septermber 19, 2019, is the water color at (46.694935, -50.925784) more milky than (46.809436, -58.528990)?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about water color in the Norwegian Sea on September 19, 2019, comparing two specific coordinates. They want to know if one location has more "milky" water than the other. For water color analysis, I should use Sentinel-2 imagery which has good water quality bands. The "milky" water likely refers to turbidity or suspended sediments. I can use: - Turbidity index or suspended matter bands - Bands that detect water clarity/color Sentinel-2 has specific water quality bands. I'll use: - Collection: COPERNICUS/S2_SR (Surface Reflectance) - Bands for water analysis: B1 (coastal aerosol), B2 (blue), B3 (green), B4 (red) - I can calculate a turbidity index or use band ratios For milky water detection, I can use: - Turbidity Index = (B4 + B3) / (B4 - B3) or similar - Or simply use reflectance in blue/green bands since milky water has higher reflectance I'll need to: 1. Define the two points 2. Get Sentinel-2 imagery for the specific date 3. Mask clouds using the QA60 band 4. Extract water reflectance values at both points 5. Compare the values to determine which is more "milky" Let me structure the code accordingly. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const point1 = ee.Geometry.Point([-50.925784, 46.694935]); const point2 = ee.Geometry.Point([-58.528990, 46.809436]); const date = '2019-09-19'; // 2. Data Acquisition - Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance const s2 = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR') .filterDate(date, ee.Date(date).advance(1, 'day')) .filterBounds(ee.Geometry.MultiPoint([point1, point2])); const s2Size = s2.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Sentinel-2 Images: ${s2Size}`); if (s2Size === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // 3. Processing - Get image and mask clouds const image = s2.first(); // Cloud masking using QA60 band const qa = image.select('QA60'); const cloudBitMask = 1 << 10; const cirrusBitMask = 1 << 11; const mask = qa.bitwiseAnd(cloudBitMask).eq(0) .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(cirrusBitMask).eq(0)); const maskedImage = image.updateMask(mask); // 4. Calculate water color index (using blue band reflectance for milky water) // Milky water typically has higher reflectance in blue/green bands const blueBand = maskedImage.select('B2'); // Blue band // 5. Extract values at both points const extractValue = function(point) { return blueBand.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: point, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('B2'); }; const val1 = extractValue(point1).getInfo(); const val2 = extractValue(point2).getInfo(); // Check for valid pixels const count1 = blueBand.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: point1.buffer(1000), scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('B2').getInfo(); const count2 = blueBand.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: point2.buffer(1000), scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('B2').getInfo(); console.log(`Point1 Blue Reflectance: ${val1}, Valid Pixels: ${count1}`); console.log(`Point2 Blue Reflectance: ${val2}, Valid Pixels: ${count2}`); // 6. Validation & Final Answer if (val1 === null || val2 === null || count1 === 0 || count2 === 0) { console.log("C2"); } else if (isNaN(val1) || isNaN(val2) || val1 === undefined || val2 === undefined) { console.log("C3"); } else { // Higher blue reflectance indicates more milky water if (val1 > val2) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
